executive_assessment.text: Provincial crop/hazard summaries and the Tandubas/Marawi workshop accounts add differentiated subnational detail, with study geography, scenario and participation limits made explicit.

The workshop describes possible climate–land/livelihood–conflict links and a reverse diversion concept. These remain low-confidence qualitative accounts; the UN workplan describes planned capacities and project status, not proven peace or adaptation outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: DA rates most priority-crop areas across the six BARMM provinces as highly climate-vulnerable.

Source dated not stated reports: Reported hazards vary: erosion/landslide across six provinces; flood in Lanao del Sur and Maguindanao provinces; surge in Basilan/Tawi-Tawi; drought in Sulu/Maguindanao del Norte.
Source dated not stated reports: Under RCP8.5, rice/coconut conditions worsen in five provinces, banana in Lanao del Sur, and coconut in Basilan; rice suitability improves in Basilan.

Source dated not stated reports: Municipalities across six provinces have generally low adaptive capacity from limited human, physical and economic capital; DA recommends crop diversification and nature-based options.
Source dated 2023-11 reports: Tandubas case notes link sea-level-related salinity/freshwater loss and inland movement to ancestral-site disputes; fishing and seaweed livelihoods were affected.
Source dated 2023-11 reports: In Marawi, participants perceived drought-linked scarcity as worsening rido and migration tensions and outstripping local capacity.
Source dated 2023-11 reports: The report links Sulu livelihood declines with harder former-combatant reintegration and reduced Basilan fishing livelihoods with recruitment.
Source dated 2026-04-15 reports: In BARMM, IDP/service advances coexist with political uncertainty, local violence, clan conflict, land disputes and service gaps.
Source dated 2026-04-15 reports: The 2026 plan supports BARMM IDP ordinances and local councils for rights-based assistance and durable solutions.
Source dated 2026-04-15 reports: The workplan lists BARMM WASH & Climate Action as under implementation in 2024–2028 across Maguindanao, Basilan, Tawi-Tawi, Sulu and Lanao del Sur.

known_gaps.text: The World Bank Philippines CCDR full report returned 403. One projected national finding is retained only from the clearly labeled official landing-page summary; assumptions and local estimates remain unverified.
The official National Adaptation Plan PDF exceeded the available fetch limit; no indexed passages were treated as evidence.
The underlying BARMM provincial CRVA reports were not inspected, so details beyond the DA webpage summary, including reference periods and municipal-level results, remain unavailable.

The strongest climate-conflict pathways are qualitative workshop case accounts from 2023, not representative or empirically tested causal estimates; the report says local residents, Indigenous communities and other vulnerable groups were not represented.
No recent quantitative study was located that estimates climate effects on violence or conflict effects on adaptation outcomes; this is an evidence-search gap, not evidence of no relationship.
The source study/workplan's BARMM groupings are retained with their vintage, not asserted as current administrative boundaries; Sulu's inclusion requires that distinction.
Qualitative recruitment and rido narratives are not treated as measured effects or generalized community threat profiles. Incomplete local/Indigenous representation limits confidence.
The conflict-resource-diversion outline is a proposed mechanism, not a verified budget loss or local operational blockage.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
